title: The Monty Hall Puzzle
objective: After this level you can explain why switching doors in the Monty Hall puzzle wins two times out of three.
summary: When a host who knows where the car is opens a goat door, switching wins 2 times in 3: your first pick was a goat 2 times in 3, and then the other closed door hides the car.

cards.headline: Three doors: one car, two goats. The host opens a goat door. Do you switch?
cards.body: It's tempting to shrug: two doors left, so why bother? In 1990 the columnist Marilyn vos Savant told Parade magazine readers to switch. Thousands of letters poured in, many from academics, insisting she was wrong. She wasn't.

cards.headline: The rule that makes the puzzle
cards.body: The puzzle is named after Monty Hall, host of the TV game show Let's Make a Deal. You pick a door. Then the host, who knows where the car is, opens one of the other two doors and shows a goat. He never opens your door, and he never reveals the car. His knowledge is the whole puzzle: the door he opens isn't random.

cards.headline: Count the three ways it can start
cards.body: Your first pick is the car 1 time in 3. Then switching loses. But 2 times in 3, your first pick is a goat. The host must open the other goat, so the only other closed door hides the car, and switching wins. Switch every time and you win 2 games in 3. Stay every time and you win 1 in 3.

mascot.line: Two doors left does not mean 50-50. The host's knowledge tipped the scales before you chose.

cards.fact: Switching wins 2 times in 3: odds of 2 to 1 in your favor.
cards.context: Another way to see it: your first door had a 1 in 3 chance, and the other two doors together had 2 in 3. When the host opens the goat among those two, that whole 2 in 3 rests on the one door he left shut. Switching is like trading your one door for both of the others.

cards.headline: Monty Hall: solved
learned: The host knows and always shows a goat
Your first pick is a goat 2 times in 3
Vos Savant, 1990: right despite thousands of letters

questions.prompt: In the Monty Hall puzzle, always switching wins the car _____.

options.label: 1 time in 2
options.rationale: Two doors are left, but they are not equally likely.

options.label: 3 times in 4
options.rationale: There are only three doors; switching wins 2 in 3.

questions.explanation: Your first pick is a goat 2 times in 3, and switching wins in every one of those games.

questions.prompt: Match each part of the Monty Hall puzzle with what happens.

pairs.left: Your first pick is the car
Your first pick is a goat

questions.explanation: If your first pick is the car, switching loses. If it's a goat, switching wins, because the host never reveals the car and must open the other goat.

questions.prompt: Switching wins 2 times in 3. Using Level 31, what are the odds in favor of a switch winning?

options.label: 2 to 3 in favor
options.rationale: Odds compare wins with losses (2 to 1), not wins with the whole.

options.label: 3 to 1 in favor
options.rationale: That would be a 3 in 4 chance.

questions.explanation: 2 wins in 3 means 2 wins to 1 loss: odds of 2 to 1 in favor.
